questions.title: Cross-Team API Disagreement
questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with another team on a technical approach.

turns.text: Tell me about a high-severity production outage you owned end to end.

Last November our checkout webhook worker backed up to 1.8 million queued events after a partner TLS rotation broke retries. I took incident command, isolated the poison-pill partner into a dead-letter shard, deployed an exponential jitter hotfix within 28 minutes, and drained the backlog with zero lost orders. Afterward I wrote an automated canary synthetic check for partner certs that caught two expirations before impact.
Tell me about a time you disagreed with another team on a technical approach.

The mobile team wanted GraphQL for order history while our platform team preferred REST. I met with their lead and explained our caching concerns, and eventually we landed on a middle ground that worked fine.

questions.title: Multi-Region Payments Ledger
questions.prompt: Design a multi-region double-entry payments ledger handling 50k TPS at <30ms p99.

turns.text: Design a multi-region double-entry payments ledger handling 50k TPS at <30ms p99.

I placed a Global API Gateway fronting our Ledger Core API, checking per-merchant token buckets in a local Redis Quota Ring under 2ms. Every mutation carries an Idempotency-Key committed atomically alongside double-entry journal rows and a transactional outbox record in Spanner, then tailed asynchronously to Kafka for settlement.

turns.text: Tell me about a subtle bug you tracked down in production.

Patient appointment reminders were firing an hour late during daylight saving transitions. I reproduced the timezone offset drift in a deterministic unit test, migrated our scheduler from naive local timestamps to UTC ISO strings with IANA zones, and cut missed-reminder support tickets from 190/week to zero. Since then I always include DST boundary fixtures in calendar tests.
Tell me about a time you had to cut scope to meet a hard deadline.
For our Q2 clinic portal launch we ran short on time for CSV export filters. I spoke with our PM and moved custom column sorting to a follow-up sprint so we could ship basic export on time.

turns.text: Tell me about a time you drove a security upgrade across reluctant product teams.

Twelve microservices still used static database passwords. I built a drop-in sidecar that leased short-lived Vault credentials with zero application code changes, paired with two teams to prove migration took under an hour, and got all 12 services rotated two weeks ahead of our SOC2 audit.
Tell me about a time you coached an engineer after a production mistake.

A mid-level engineer accidentally pushed an overly broad IAM policy to staging that broke CI deploys for three hours. Instead of taking over, I paired with them to trace the least-privilege diff, let them lead the blameless postmortem, and together we added an OPA policy check in PR CI. They later owned our entire IAM linting suite and zero broad policies shipped in the next 9 months. It reinforced for me that pairing on guardrails builds far more ownership than top-down reviews.
